concepts.name: A flower is the reproductive structure of angiosperms containing male and female reproductive organs
learning_points: Identify sepals, petals, stamens and carpels

concepts.name: Microsporogenesis is the formation of haploid microspores from diploid microspore mother cells through meiosis
Megasporogenesis produces megaspores from the megaspore mother cell and leads to development of the female gametophyte
learning_points: Identify egg apparatus, polar nuclei and antipodals

concepts.name: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma and may occur within or between flowers
Angiosperms exhibit double fertilisation involving syngamy and triple fusion
After fertilisation, the zygote and primary endosperm nucleus develop into embryo and endosperm while ovule and ovary develop into seed and fruit
Apomixis and polyembryony are specialised reproductive phenomena that can produce seeds or multiple embryos through unusual developmental pathways
The male reproductive system produces sperm and reproductive hormones and provides pathways for sperm transport
The female reproductive system produces ova, supports fertilisation and provides the environment for embryo development
Gametogenesis produces haploid male and female gametes through coordinated cell division and differentiation
The menstrual cycle involves coordinated ovarian, uterine and hormonal changes that prepare for possible pregnancy
learning_points: Relate FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone

concepts.name: Fertilisation forms a diploid zygote that undergoes cleavage and eventually implants in the uterine wall
Pregnancy involves coordinated development of embryo and foetus supported by placenta and maternal physiological changes
Parturition is childbirth and lactation is milk production regulated by hormonal mechanisms
Reproductive health includes physical, mental and social well-being related to reproductive systems and processes
Contraception prevents pregnancy through methods that interfere with fertilisation, implantation or reproductive processes
Medical termination of pregnancy is a regulated medical procedure with medical, ethical and legal considerations
learning_points: Understand importance of legal and ethical safeguards

concepts.name: Sexually transmitted infections can spread through sexual contact and may affect reproductive and general health
Assisted reproductive technologies help overcome certain causes of infertility using medically assisted reproductive processes
Mendelian genetics explains inheritance patterns using discrete hereditary factors and predictable segregation and assortment
A monohybrid cross follows inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits
A dihybrid cross follows inheritance of two pairs of contrasting traits and demonstrates independent assortment under appropriate conditions
Genes are located on chromosomes and chromosomal behaviour during meiosis provides a physical basis for Mendelian inheritance
Genes located on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together but crossing over can produce recombinant combinations
learning_points: Relate recombination frequency to gene distance

concepts.name: Sex determination in different organisms can depend on specific chromosomal or environmental mechanisms
Mutations and chromosomal changes can alter genetic information and may produce inherited disorders
DNA is a double-stranded nucleic acid whose complementary nucleotide sequence stores hereditary information
DNA is compacted through association with proteins into higher-order chromatin structures
DNA replication produces two DNA molecules, each containing one parental and one newly synthesised strand
Transcription copies genetic information from DNA into RNA using complementary base pairing
The genetic code maps nucleotide triplets in mRNA to amino acids during protein synthesis
Translation uses ribosomes, mRNA, tRNA and amino acids to synthesise polypeptide chains
Gene expression can be regulated through molecular mechanisms that control transcription in response to cellular conditions
Molecular biology techniques allow analysis, comparison and practical use of genomic DNA
Evolutionary biology examines how life originated and diversified over geological time
learning_points: Understand theories of origin of life
Understand experimental evidence related to origin of life

concepts.name: Fossils, comparative anatomy, embryology, molecular biology and biogeography provide evidence for common ancestry and evolutionary change
Natural selection explains evolutionary change through differential survival and reproduction of individuals with heritable variations
Modern evolutionary theory integrates natural selection with genetics, mutation, recombination, gene flow and genetic drift
The Hardy-Weinberg principle describes allele and genotype frequencies in an ideal population without evolutionary forces
Adaptive radiation occurs when related organisms diversify into different ecological niches
learning_points: Use Darwin's finches as an example
Understand Australian marsupials as an example

concepts.name: Human evolution involved a branching sequence of ancestral populations with changes in anatomy, behaviour and culture
learning_points: Understand major stages of human evolution

concepts.name: Disease results from disturbances in normal body function and can arise from infectious or non-infectious causes
Different pathogens cause characteristic diseases through specific modes of transmission and mechanisms
The immune system protects the body through innate defences and antigen-specific adaptive responses
learning_points: Understand primary and secondary immune responses

concepts.name: Vaccination exposes the immune system to suitable antigenic material to generate protective immune memory
Allergies are exaggerated immune responses to otherwise harmless substances
HIV infection progressively impairs immune function by targeting important immune cells
Cancer involves abnormal uncontrolled proliferation and may result from genetic and environmental factors
Psychoactive substances can alter nervous-system function and may lead to dependence and serious health consequences

chapters.title: Human Reproduction and Reproductive Health Applications

concepts.name: Modern reproductive technologies can assist conception and address selected causes of infertility
Prenatal diagnostic methods can identify certain developmental or genetic conditions but require strict ethical and legal safeguards

chapters.title: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production

concepts.name: Animal husbandry applies scientific principles to breeding, feeding and management of domesticated animals
Plant breeding develops improved crop varieties by selecting and combining desirable hereditary traits
Hybridisation crosses genetically different parents to combine useful characteristics in offspring
Plant tissue culture uses controlled conditions to regenerate plants from small pieces of plant tissue
Apiculture and fisheries use scientific management to increase production of useful animal resources
Microorganisms are used in controlled fermentation processes to produce food and useful products
Microorganisms produce commercially important compounds including organic acids, alcohols and enzymes
Microorganisms help degrade organic matter during biological treatment of sewage
Anaerobic microbial communities convert organic matter into biogas containing methane and other gases
Biocontrol uses living organisms or their products to manage pests and pathogens
Biofertilisers use beneficial microorganisms to improve nutrient availability and soil fertility
Biotechnology applies biological systems, organisms or components to develop useful products and processes
Recombinant DNA technology combines DNA sequences from different sources and propagates selected genetic material
Restriction endonucleases recognise specific DNA sequences and cleave DNA at or near those sites
Cloning vectors carry foreign DNA into host cells and provide features required for replication and selection
PCR exponentially amplifies a selected DNA sequence through repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing and extension
Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments primarily according to size under an electric field
Bioreactors provide controlled conditions for large-scale growth of cells or microorganisms and production of biological products
Genetic modification changes an organism's genetic material to introduce desired characteristics
Genetic engineering can introduce traits such as pest resistance or improved nutritional characteristics into crops
Genetic engineering enables production of medically useful proteins in suitable biological systems
Gene therapy attempts to treat disease by introducing, modifying or regulating genetic material in target cells
Molecular diagnostic techniques detect pathogens, genetic variants or disease-associated molecules with high specificity
Biotechnology applications require scientific, ethical, environmental and regulatory evaluation
Organisms interact continuously with physical and biological factors in their environment
A population has measurable attributes such as density, birth rate, death rate and age distribution
Population size changes according to birth, death, immigration and emigration and can follow different mathematical growth patterns
Species interact through relationships such as predation, competition, parasitism, mutualism and commensalism
Adaptations are structural, physiological or behavioural features that improve survival and reproduction in particular environments
An ecosystem consists of interacting biotic communities and abiotic environmental components
Productivity measures the rate at which organic matter is produced in an ecosystem
learning_points: Distinguish gross and net primary productivity

concepts.name: Decomposition converts complex organic matter into simpler substances through detritivores and decomposers
Energy flows through ecosystems from producers to consumers and is progressively lost as heat

subtopics.name: Pyramids of number, biomass and energy

concepts.name: Ecological pyramids represent quantitative relationships among trophic levels
Matter moves between organisms and the physical environment through interconnected nutrient cycles
Biodiversity encompasses variation at genetic, species and ecosystem levels
Biodiversity varies across geographic regions and generally follows recognisable ecological patterns
Human activities can cause biodiversity loss through habitat destruction, overexploitation, invasive species and other pressures

subtopics.name: In situ and ex situ conservation

concepts.name: Biodiversity can be conserved within natural habitats or outside them using managed conservation facilities
Biodiversity hotspots are regions with exceptional biodiversity and significant levels of threat
Air pollution occurs when harmful substances enter the atmosphere at concentrations that adversely affect organisms and the environment
Water pollution degrades water quality through biological, chemical and physical contaminants
Solid waste requires appropriate collection, treatment, recovery and disposal to minimise environmental impacts
Increased concentrations of greenhouse gases enhance heat retention in Earth's atmosphere and contribute to climate change
Certain chemicals can catalytically destroy stratospheric ozone, reducing protection from ultraviolet radiation
Deforestation alters ecosystems, biodiversity, soil, water cycles and climate
Environmental protection combines scientific management, legislation, conservation and sustainable use of natural resources
learning_points: Understand environmental impact of human activities
